transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-02 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Leah Patel (Summit - Head of Compliance), Omar Siddiqui (Summit - Cloud Architect), Priya Mehta (Summit - PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Summit wants to understand cross-border data flows, operator access controls, and logging retention for use cases that handle payment instrument and KYC PII. Exploring Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC or on-prem) for GDPR/HIPAA constraints. Key asks: where logs live, whether model prompt/response content leaves region, KMS integration and key residency, and ability to redact tokens from logs. Next steps: share compliance docs, architecture deep dive, trial tenant in EU.

Topics: data residency, operator access, KMS key residency, logging retention and redaction, SOC2/HIPAA posture, cost/latency tradeoffs, pilot setup.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call and then we'll jump in — I'm Avery, account lead at Redwood. Marco, you want to intro?
[00:10] Marco Ruiz: Yeah hi, Marco Ruiz, solutions engineer. I'll focus on architecture and security questions.
[00:15] Leah Patel: Leah here, Head of Compliance at Summit. Thanks for the invite. We have Omar and Priya with us as well.
[00:21] Omar Siddiqui: Hey all.
[00:23] Priya Mehta: Hi.
[00:25] Avery Chen: Great. Our goal today is to map how data flows in the Hosted product versus Dedicated and Private, and confirm controls around operator access and logs. We'll leave 10 minutes at the end for next steps. Sound good?
[00:34] Leah Patel: Yep fine.
[00:36] Priya Mehta: Works for us.
[00:38] Avery Chen: Cool. Quick context from Summit — Priya, can you run through the main workloads?
[00:45] Priya Mehta: Sure. We have two main features: a KYC intake assistant that summarizes uploaded identity docs and flags high risk items, and a payments reconciliation chat that can show masked card-ending results and suggest routing. Both features send PII-ish content to model inference. We need strict control on residency for EU customers and HIPAA-ish controls for healthcare-linked merchant verticals.
[01:10] Avery Chen: Understood. Omar, what is your current infra footprint and any constraints?
[01:15] Omar Siddiqui: We're primarily on GCP in us-west1 and europe-west1. We use customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, and we currently have strict VPC peering rules — no public egress for certain subsystems. We also have a security requirement that only a subset of ops engineers can see raw user-generated content or logs that contain PII.
[01:32] Marco Ruiz: ok, good data. A couple of quick callouts: Hosted runs in multi-tenant environments with region selection for processing, Dedicated provides reserved capacity but still managed by Redwood, and Private gives you either a VPC-based control plane or a deployable on-prem package where logs and keys can remain under your control. We'll dive into specifics.
[01:53] Leah Patel: When you say "region selection for processing" for Hosted, does that guarantee that data never leaves europe-west? GDPR requires that for certain customers we cannot have cross-border processing without legal basis.
[02:06] Marco Ruiz: Good question. For Hosted, we provide region pinning so requests for EU-labeled customers are processed in europe-west1 hardware. However, there are some background services — for example, telemetry aggregates and billing — that may be routed to our control plane in us-central. We can put contracts in place and provide data processing addenda covering lawful transfer mechanisms.
[02:28] Leah Patel: And are request/response payloads stored in any cross-region logs by default?
[02:34] Marco Ruiz: By default, short-term inference logs — to support reruns and debugging — are stored for up to 7 days in the processing region, but some aggregated traces and usage metrics are retained in our central analytics. We have options to disable payload logging and keep only token counts and latencies.
[02:50] Omar Siddiqui: Can you disable the storage of raw prompt/response payloads completely? We can't have customer PII persisted outside our control.
[02:58] Marco Ruiz: For Hosted, we can disable payload persistence at the tenant level — that means we won't persist prompt/response content after the request completes. However, there is still transient in-memory storage and cache (the KV cache) used for streaming; that does not persist to disk if configured that way. If you need absolute guarantee of no operator visibility and no cross-region copies, the Private deployment inside your VPC or our on-prem will be the recommended path.
[03:24] Leah Patel: What about operator access for emergency debugging? For incidents, sometimes Redwood engineers might need to look at traces. How is that controlled?
[03:32] Marco Ruiz: We use role-based access controls and an access workflow. For Hosted, operator access to payloads is strictly audited; access requests require justification and are time-limited. We also support a "no-operator-access" policy for enterprise tenants where we restrict human access unless explicit legal or emergency approvals are provided.
[03:48] Leah Patel: Audited is fine but we need to see the audit records. Can you provide audit logs?
[03:54] Marco Ruiz: Yes, audit logs are available. We can include them in the contract and show sample entries. For Private, those logs remain in your environment entirely.
[04:03] Priya Mehta: Regarding KMS: does Redwood support customer-managed keys and can keys be kept in europe-only key stores?
[04:11] Marco Ruiz: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we have a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integration for certain tiers where your keys live in your cloud KMS and we request decryption tokens. For region residency guarantees you'd want the KMS and the processing region to be co-located — Private/VPC is simplest for that.
[04:28] Avery Chen: I'll add that for BYOK flows in Hosted we still have to orchestrate ephemeral keys for the runtime, so some metadata may transit our control plane. We can provide data flow diagrams.
[04:40] Leah Patel: Metadata transit is ok if it's limited, but we need to confirm there is no plaintext PII in metadata or logs that leave the EU.
[04:48] Marco Ruiz: Understood, we can redact and hash identifiers in metadata and provide a sample scrub config.
[04:55] Omar Siddiqui: How about retention — what's configurable? We have a security policy of a max 30 day retention for anything that could contain PII, ideally shorter.
[05:04] Marco Ruiz: Defaults are 7 days for raw payloads (if enabled) and 180 days for aggregated traces. We can change those SLOs via enterprise agreement. We also offer redaction-in-flight and tokenization hooks to avoid storing sensitive fields.
[05:20] Leah Patel: On the HIPAA side, do you sign BAA? Is the Hosted product BAA-eligible?
[05:27] Avery Chen: We sign BAAs for enterprise contracts and have a HIPAA controls map. Hosted can be covered under a BAA commitment for specific accounts, but again, if you need strict tenant isolation and dedicated logging under your control, Dedicated or Private might be preferable.
[05:41] Leah Patel: Okay. For financial controls — PCI scope — we can't have full card numbers leaving our environment. We would rely on tokenization and redaction. Is there an official PCI guidance?
[05:53] Marco Ruiz: We don't handle card PANs in plaintext; we recommend tokenization and field-level redaction before sending to inference. For some customers we integrate with a customer-side tokenization service so the model sees only masked values. We can also provide a whitepaper mapping how to keep PCI out of our logs.
[06:09] Priya Mehta: If we redact client-submitted docs client-side, does that impact model performance? For KYC summarization we sometimes need to see certain fields to validate identity.
[06:19] Marco Ruiz: Right — there's a tradeoff. You can do deterministic redaction and pass hashed placeholders plus a small context extractor that runs in your environment to surface necessary attributes. Another option is Private so the model can operate on unredacted inputs inside your VPC. We'll show benchmarking on both.
[06:34] Omar Siddiqui: Let's talk about operator-level key access. If we use customer-managed KMS, can Redwood staff decrypt logs for debugging?
[06:42] Marco Ruiz: With CUSTOMER-MANAGED keys, Redwood does not have the key material. Any decryption would require an explicit grant from your KMS. We can do an access flow where you temporarily grant a cryptographic access token that is audited and expires.
[06:56] Leah Patel: That flow sounds promising. We need to see the exact permissions required and whether our security team is comfortable with the ephemeral grant model.
[07:04] Marco Ruiz: We'll include the IAM action list in the follow-up.
[07:08] Priya Mehta: About logs — is it possible to keep full debug logs locally only and send only aggregates to Redwood for billing and capacity planning?
[07:17] Marco Ruiz: Yes, for Private deployments you can ship only metrics upstream and keep full logs on-prem. For Dedicated we can configure log forwarding rules so raw payloads never leave your environment — only summarized metrics are sent to Redwood. 
[07:33] Leah Patel: Can you confirm the level of SOC/ISO certifications and if there's a penetration testing report we can see?
[07:40] Avery Chen: We are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; we can share the latest report under NDA. We also have third-party pen test summaries.
[07:50] Omar Siddiqui: Any geography-specific proof for EU processing? Do you have EU legal counsel sign-offs or SCCs?
[07:58] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we have Standard Contractual Clauses in place and a data processing addendum. For Private installs inside your EU project, SCCs are not needed because processing stays in region.
[08:09] Leah Patel: Good. I want to probe a little bit on transient caches — you mentioned K-V cache. Is that persisted anywhere?
[08:16] Marco Ruiz: The KV cache is in-memory for the runtime; it doesn't persist to disk by default, but some of our optimizations write checkpoints that can be configured to avoid writing sensitive tokens. We can turn off checkpoints for sensitive tenants.
[08:29] Priya Mehta: Are there any regulatory bodies you've onboarded specifically in payments that might require specific audit trails?
[08:36] Avery Chen: We haven't done payment-regulator-specific attestations as a vendor, most customers build controls around tokenization and redaction. But we have experience supporting audits for large customers and providing audit packages.
[08:50] Leah Patel: Regarding SLAs — if we go Dedicated, do you provide stronger latency and availability SLAs?
[08:57] Marco Ruiz: Dedicated comes with committed capacity and a higher SLA for latency and throughput, yes. Private can be aligned to your own infra SLAs.
[09:06] Omar Siddiqui: Cost question — how different is Dedicated vs Hosted in price profile? Rough order of magnitude?
[09:12] Avery Chen: Dedicated is higher baseline (reserved capacity) but lower marginal cost per token. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with slightly higher per-token rates. We'll send a pricing sketch but baseline depends on model size and qps.
[09:24] Leah Patel: Another compliance question — do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning? We want to limit which engineers can trigger debug access.
[09:33] Marco Ruiz: Yes SSO via SAML, SSO provisioning, RBAC, and audit trails. We can integrate with your IdP and restrict roles.
[09:40] Priya Mehta: Let's touch on logs redaction automation. Can we provide a list of fields to be redacted and have Redwood apply redaction before persisting?
[09:49] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we have redaction rules — regex-based or schema-based — that run pre-persistence. We'll include sample config.
[09:56] Leah Patel: On data subject rights (GDPR) — if a user requests deletion, how do you guarantee elimination from backups and logs?
[10:05] Marco Ruiz: We have data deletion flows and can run targeted deletion for tenant data; we can also provide a documented SLA for deletion propagation. For backups, we can tag datasets and exclude from long-term backups or rotate them to achieve deletion windows.
[10:19] Priya Mehta: For the pilot, we want to validate latency for EU customers and also confirm that logs and KMS flows satisfy our security policy. Can Redwood spin up a EU-only test tenant?
[10:28] Marco Ruiz: Yes, we can provision a short-lived EU-only tenant for a 2-week pilot. We'll map what metrics you'll want and set up an architecture deep-dive.
[10:36] Avery Chen: Great. Leah, Omar, Priya — anything else critical we haven't covered?
[10:41] Leah Patel: A few quick items: 1) sample audit log entries, 2) the exact IAM permissions required for temporary KMS grants, and 3) a redaction rule example.
[10:50] Omar Siddiqui: Also a sample cost estimate for Dedicated RU per qps and the expected token latencies for our model sizes.
[10:58] Marco Ruiz: Noted. We'll prepare those.
[11:02] Priya Mehta: Might be helpful to see a demo of Private in a VPC in terms of setup complexity.
[11:08] Avery Chen: We can schedule a setup workshop.
[11:11] [Silence / crosstalk]
[11:15] Leah Patel: Also curious about deletion of derivable embeddings — if you derive embeddings from PII, do you persist them?
[11:22] Marco Ruiz: Embeddings are considered derivative data and can be configured to not be stored. Default is to store embeddings for similarity workloads, but we can disable.
[11:31] Omar Siddiqui: One more — for compliance, we might require key escrow or legal hold procedures. Do you support key escrow?
[11:38] Marco Ruiz: We don't offer key escrow out of the box. For Private installs you can configure your own escrow solutions. For Hosted, we can discuss bespoke arrangements for large enterprise.
[11:49] Leah Patel: Ok thanks. Let's do recap and next steps.
[11:53] Avery Chen: Recap: Redwood to share SOC2/HIPAA/DPA and SCC docs, Marco to share architecture sketch and IAM actions, Austin? I mean Avery will send pricing sheet and pilot proposal, Summit to share traffic profile and sample PII templates. We'll provision EU-only pilot tenant for two weeks.
[12:15] Omar Siddiqui: Sounds good.
[12:17] Priya Mehta: Thanks everyone.
[12:18] Avery Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up within 48 hours.

End of meeting.

Notes about transcription: there were a few misheard product names (one reference to "Redwood Privy" instead of Private), filler words, and overlapping talk in a couple spots.
